label: <DEL> step when the original sequence is rich in f/o/j/z (and c/p/q/t/0/3)
explanation: Almost exclusively a delimiter-step unit: 86% of activations and 92% of activation mass are at the <DEL> step (t == L), where it fires on about 11% of sequences. Whether it fires there depends on what fraction of the original tokens come from a preferred set, mainly f, o, j, z, and more weakly c, p, q, t, 0, 3. Short sequences (L 3-6) fire more often than long ones. A weighted-count predicate (2x f/o/j/z plus the broader set, at least L) gets dev F1 0.47 and mass recall 0.76. Top-quartile activations are covered best (about 97% by phase==1 alone), and the top examples are sequences made almost entirely of f/o/j. Activations elsewhere are weak and scattered: copy steps (8% of mass, mostly recall_idx 2-3, often the first copy output) and a negligible amount in the original phase. It never fires at t<3. Precision is limited because the token-composition dependence is graded, and a simple set count does not reproduce the threshold.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig2=f (+2.89), orig2=j (+2.56), orig2=o (+2.51), orig3=f (+2.46), orig3=j (+2.30), orig3=o (+2.26). Lower it: in_tok=f (-3.94), in_tok=o (-3.80), in_tok=j (-3.53), in_tok=z (-3.32).
